brewing.notes: A safe starting point for dark tea: rinse once, boiling water, or simmer it the traditional way.

description:
A Mongolian drink of crumbled brick tea boiled in an iron pot with milk and salt, drunk through the day and offered to guests. Fried millet, butter or tail fat are common additions.

This is a way of preparing tea more than a tea you buy under one name, so the recipe and the base tea change from one maker to the next.
history: By one account, herders began boiling tea with fresh milk after Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty, when tea reached them. In the mid-thirteenth century the friar William of Rubruck recorded that Mongols took care not to drink plain water, a habit that favoured milk drinks.
processing: Brick tea is broken up and boiled in water, then milk and salt are added and it is brought back to the boil; traditionally it is scooped and poured back from a height.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: it depends on the base tea.
appearance_dry: Usually dark leaf, loose or pressed into bricks or baskets.
appearance_wet: Usually coarse dark leaf with some stem.
taste_profile: Salty and creamy, varying by region and household.
vintage_note: Not sold by vintage: it is made from whatever base tea the maker keeps, so freshness of the base matters more than the year.
